title: Application for Federal Domestic Assistance- Individual
description: Application for Federal Domestic Assistance - Individual (SF424_Individual_2_0) collects application information from individual applicants seeking federal domestic assistance. Unlike other SF-424 variants, this form has no organization, EIN, or estimated funding sections -- the applicant IS the individual. It captures the applicant's name, address, contact information, citizenship status, project details, and certification. This is the simplest form in the SF-424 family, designed exclusively for individual (non-organizational) applicants.
notes: State requirement: DAT describes State as "required if Country is the United States." The XSD marks State as optional (within AddressDataTypeV3, minOccurs="0"). Resolution: follow the XSD. State is conditionally required only when Country is USA, enforced at the UI level.

ZIP/Postal Code requirement: DAT says ZIP is "required if the country is the United States" with minimum 9 characters for US addresses. The XSD marks ZipPostalCode as optional (minOccurs="0"). Resolution: follow the XSD for XML validation; enforce the US-specific rule at the UI level.

Citizenship conditional fields: DAT says Country of Citizenship and Residency Start Date are "required" when citizenship = No, but the XSD marks both as optional (minOccurs="0"). Resolution: follow the XSD for XML validation; enforce the conditional requirement at the UI level.
No organization fields: Unlike all other SF-424 variants, this form has no organization name, EIN/TIN, department, division, or UEI fields in the XSD. The applicant is the individual directly.

AOR has name only: The `AuthorizedRepresentativeName` element uses `HumanNameDataType` (Prefix, FirstName, MiddleName, LastName, Suffix) with no accompanying title, phone, email, fax, or organization fields, unlike other SF-424 variants where the AOR section includes full contact information. Phone, email, and fax exist as separate top-level elements.
ZIP/Postal Code maxLength: The XSD defines ZipPostalCodeDataType with maxLength 30. We will use the XSD constraint (30) for validation.
Province maxLength: The XSD defines ProvinceDataType with maxLength 30. We will use the XSD constraint (30) for validation.

XSD element naming: The XSD uses `AuthorizedRepresentativeName`, `AuthorizedRepresentativePhoneNumber`, `AuthorizedRepresentativeEmail`, and `AuthorizedRepresentativeFax` for the individual applicant's own information. The JSON paths use `applicant.*` for clarity while maintaining the correct XML element mapping.
risks: This is the only SF-424 variant designed for individual (non-organizational) applicants. It cannot be combined with organizational SF-424 forms in the same application package.

The citizenship section has three distinct states: US citizen, permanent resident (with alien registration number), and foreign national (with country/date). The XSD uses a simple YesNoDataType for the `citizenship` element, so the UI should handle this as a multi-step conditional flow, not a simple Yes/No.

The XSD element names reference "AuthorizedRepresentative" but this form has no separate AOR. The applicant IS the representative. The JSON model uses clearer naming (e.g., `applicant.*`) while maintaining correct XML mapping.

The XSD element sequence places `AuthorizedRepresentativeFax` before `AuthorizedRepresentativeEmail` and `AuthorizedRepresentativePhoneNumber`, which is unusual and does not match the DAT section order. XML generation must follow the XSD sequence.
The citizenship section collects sensitive personal information (alien registration number). Ensure appropriate data handling and privacy protections.
